## Shared context (verbatim, immutable)

# Verification-integrity final full review

Review the complete `06efaae43c0f343efc6e2bb6c289b907b218b9be..ece0c43eeaa80b9d385176f151ff52354ba3e8e8` diff and every changed file read-only. The implementer is Kimi; this review covers verification-infrastructure contracts, Python implementation and tests, review instructions, and the temporarily stale ledger note that will be corrected after final assurance.

Settled earlier findings, all with before-failing and after-passing regressions:
- Imported, aliased, decorated, and wildcard pytest suppressions are resolved; combined wildcard imports from both pytest and pytest.mark now retain every source.
- Comments cannot hide equal operands; exact string/regex literal whitespace remains significant.
- Repeated calls and other potentially side-effecting operands are not assumed equal.
- TypeScript expect toBe/toEqual/toStrictEqual scans cover nonliteral self-comparisons and trailing commas.
- Whole newly allocated object/array/regex literals are exempt only for identity matchers; member expressions and deep-equality structural comparisons remain V5.
- Plain template literals and backticks inside strings are not tagged templates; tagged-template detection uses masked code.
- The three-model review rule is maintainer-directed and settled.
- GitHub server enforcement and ledger correction are tracked separately; do not re-report them as repository-code findings.

The e4814ef9 refactor passed verification with no oracle edits. The final refactoring run applied only mechanical renames in ece0c43e and verified no oracle edits with growth ratio 0.1656; structural suggestions rejected for growth ratio, unnecessary abstraction, or V4 caller attribution are settled. Focus on concrete behavioral defects, contract drift, ineffective tests, baseline subtraction, parsing offsets, alias scoping, and equality semantics. Return at most five findings with triggers and observable consequences, or an empty findings list promptly.

summary: 审查了完整变更中的验证完整性检查器、测试与契约，重点验证别名作用域、比较语义、侧效应过滤和基线行为。发现 5 个可复现缺陷：两类静默绕过和三类误报，均会直接破坏 V3/V5 的可信度或阻断合法测试。

findings.title: Java class literals bypass the V5 self-comparison check
findings.trigger: A head change replaces an existing Java assertion with `assertEquals(Foo.class, Foo.class)` or `assertSame(String.class, String.class)` while preserving the assertion count.
findings.consequence: The always-passing self-comparison produces no V5 violation and the integrity gate exits 0, accepting a permanently vacuous assertion as verification evidence.
findings.evidence: `C_LIKE_SIDE_EFFECT` treats every `class` token as side-effecting at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:271; `self_comparing` therefore returns false at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:289-291; the Java caller consequently never sets `noop` at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:398.
findings.suggestedFix: Use language-aware purity detection and treat a Java type literal such as `Foo.class` as side-effect-free, for example by excluding `.<identifier>class` from the Java side-effect scan. Add a V5 regression for class literals.

findings.title: V5 misses equivalent TypeScript strings with different quote styles
findings.trigger: A new assertion uses semantically identical literals with different delimiters, such as `assert.strictEqual("x", 'x')` or `expect("x").toEqual('x')`.
findings.consequence: The assertion always passes, but no V5 violation is emitted, so replacing a meaningful assertion with this form preserves the count and bypasses the integrity gate.
findings.evidence: `comparison_form` preserves the complete literal span including its delimiters at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:259-266, making `"x"` and `'x'` unequal before `self_comparing` is reached. The new TypeScript callers at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:604 and :616 therefore miss the no-op.
findings.suggestedFix: Parse and compare the runtime value of non-interpolated TypeScript string literals, such as by decoding escapes and ignoring single/double/backtick delimiter choice while retaining exact regex contents. Add mixed-quote regressions.

findings.title: Calls inside template substitutions escape side-effect filtering
findings.trigger: A TypeScript assertion uses a plain template with repeated side-effecting substitutions, for example `expect(`${Math.random()}`).toBe(`${Math.random()}`)`.
findings.consequence: The two expressions may evaluate differently, but the gate reports V5 and blocks a legitimate test.
findings.evidence: The masking loop blanks the entire backtick literal at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:186-200, including all `${...}` expressions. `self_comparing` then inspects only the blanked `source.code` at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:289-291, while `comparison_form` sees identical raw template text.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat template substitution expressions as code while masking only cooked template text. Skip V5 when substitutions contain calls, updates, assignments, or other side effects, and add regressions for both pure and side-effecting substitutions.

findings.title: Calls with type arguments are misclassified as pure self-comparisons
findings.trigger: A new assertion calls a generic method or function on both sides, such as `expect(factory.create<string>()).toBe(factory.create<string>())` or Java `assertEquals(factory.<String>create(), factory.<String>create())`.
findings.consequence: Repeated calls may have side effects or return different values, but the gate reports V5 and rejects a legitimate test.
findings.evidence: `C_LIKE_CALL` at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:272 recognizes only `name(` and misses type arguments between the name and parentheses. `self_comparing` consequently reaches its success return at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:300; both Java and TypeScript callers depend on this result at :398 and :604/:616.
findings.suggestedFix: Use token-aware call detection that supports type arguments and member access, or extend the call matcher to cover balanced `<...>` between callable names and `(` without mistaking relational expressions for generics. Add Java and TypeScript regressions.

findings.title: File-global pytest alias resolution ignores lexical shadowing
findings.trigger: A file imports `from pytest import skip as suppress`, but a test locally reassigns or defines `suppress = str` (or a nested `def suppress`) and calls `suppress("ordinary")`.
findings.consequence: The call is not a suppression at runtime, yet the scanner emits a new V3 violation and CI rejects the legitimate test.
findings.evidence: `python_pytest_imports` walks the entire module with `ast.walk` and stores one global alias map at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:439-453. `python_resolved_name` applies that alias without checking assignments, local definitions, import order, or lexical scope at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:456-462; the runtime call scan then reports V3 at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:545-548.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve names with lexical scope and execution order, honoring local imports, assignments, parameter bindings, class scopes, and shadowing before classifying a call as pytest suppression. Add shadowed-alias regressions.
